2518d488: Outputs a leading blank line followed by the DLB_" string and a space.
9246eba4: Ends execution of the current routine/module.
61cdebab: Handles word-wrapping of the Y variable. If Y doesn't fit on the current line, it writes a newline and outputs a tab.
4561f515: Checks if the input variable Y is longer than 19 characters and if certain conditions related to DV are met. If so, it branches to the RW^DIR2 routine/label.
dbea0bc7: Outputs the "// " string if Y is not empty. If DV is not defined and DV["I"] is true and DE(DQ) exists, it sets X to an empty string and outputs "  (No Editing)" before quitting.
f282445c: Reads user input into X within a specified DTIME timeout. If a timeout occurs, it sets DTOUT to the up-arrow character and X to the up-arrow character. It also outputs a beep character.
6ee5ffca: Ends execution of the current routine/module.
bfc72de0: Count the current array element for $G branching.
a3deef27: Branch to the array element counted by DQ.
5830f16b: Go to the PR label if a new record is being edited, otherwise process the input and do transforms.
7e710cd6: If no input, branch based on DV value and whether a new record is being created.
aa25a962: If input is a '?', go to the QS label for help, otherwise if it starts with '^' process the jump.
01815bc9: If input is '@', jump to the Z^DIE2 label.
da3baf32: If input is a space and the data is a set of codes, get the previously entered value and display it.

1a9651ad: Branch based on DV value. If DV is defined, go to M^DIE17. If DV contains 'V', go to ^DIE3. If DV does not contain 'S', go to P. Otherwise, execute any executable help and check the input against DIC('S'). If valid, display any transform and go to V.
dadb9cf0: Loop through set of multiple entries in DU. Execute any DIC('S') code against each entry and quit the loop if a match is found.
d1562937: Display the remainder of the matched entry from DU if no word-processing field is being edited. Set X to the matched entry.
ce2191f3: Perform lookup in NEW Person file if file prefix is P;
cab74a87: For a new entry, if .01 field value is numeric and longer than 24 digits, then quit without setting X;
5fccbf13: If a numeric value with decimal is entered and word-processing is off, strip leading and trailing zeros, remove decimal point if no decimal portion;
a86fd2bf: Execute COMPUTED-FIELD expression to set X and kill YS;
b3364bad: If X was set, store it in ^UTILITY for auditing if DV contains 'd' (AUDIT-TRAIL), then quit.
03ef49d2: If the data dictionary is present, branch to the routine DIE17.
30e95c82: Set X to an error value indicating bad data.
98560745: Set DZ to X, call D to set up data for the current field, call QQ^DIEQ to print the field value, then go to label B.
cae66ded: Set up variables for the current field: D=field number, DQ(DQ)=field attributes, and get the DIEDIT parameter for the field (the .01 node of the DD).
ee169c56: If the field does not have DIEDIT parameters: if X is not '@', branch to RD; if DV does not contain 'R' and X is '@', branch to A; if X is '@', set X to Y and branch to N.
149b1aae: Set DG to DV, Y to the DIEDIT parameters for the field, and X to the user input. If there is a DIEDIT transform, execute it. Then go to RP.
64d60d6c: Set X to the compiled piece (field number) and lookup in file ^DD(X,.01,0) to get a node value and go to RP if no relational data.
e1562f2b: If Y is a variable pointer reference, lookup the pointed-to file number (X), get the .01 field data, set DG to the compiled piece and get the node value, then go to R.
dcaac753: Execute DD utility and set Y to subfile number if it exists and DG indicates subfile data.

If successful, the value is stored in X and OUT^DIE17 is branched to. If the value is undefined or null (U), branch to A.
